$comment: Machine-readable expected coverage for the Irwin gold eval. This is a FLOOR, not a fixed answer key: a run may exceed or reorder it when evidence supports doing so, but must explain every deviation. Scoring is semantic — a run is judged on whether it explains these things, never on whether it reproduces the brief's sentences.

failIf: Identity is resolved from the LLM rather than from a real bibliographic lookup.
Any of the fields above is guessed when the lookup did not return it.

expectedSectionTitles: A Gap in Aristotle's Moral Psychology
Pursuing the Expedient without the Fine
The Instability of the Vicious Person
expectedStructure.note: Section titles were recovered from the fixture's own text layer (see verification.sectionStructure). A degraded/structure-limited run FAILS this fixture.

expectedArguments.must: State the puzzle: the vicious act on decision (prohairesis), which implies rational guidance, yet are said to live according to passion rather than reason.
Distinguish vice from akrasia: the vicious act ON decision, the akratic AGAINST decision.
Explain Irwin's solution: reason remains active in vice but is subordinated to antecedent inclination — strategic/instrumental rather than authoritative over ends.
Explain that the virtuous agent chooses for the sake of the kalon (the fine), as against the vicious agent's orientation to the expedient/advantageous.
Connect vice to the pursuit of pleasure.
Explain the particular kind of regret characteristic of the vicious person.
Explain the instability of the vicious person and defective self-love.
Surface Irwin's own admission that he develops Aristotle's remarks 'beyond anything he says'.
expectedArguments.why: This is the paper's own epistemic hedge. Presenting Irwin's reconstruction as straight Aristotle exegesis without it is a substantive failure.

expectedArguments.must: Surface the closing scope caveat: the account fits cowardice, intemperance, AND SLOTH better than greed, vindictiveness, and the desire for power and domination.
expectedArguments.why: The reference brief omits sloth. A run that also omits it is echoing the brief rather than reading the paper.

expectedArguments.must: Present the strongest interpretive objections to Irwin's unifying account — principally that the unifying mechanism leans hard on his reading of the kalon and on a strong fine/advantageous split, which is exactly where Müller and non-intellectualist readings resist him.

expectedScholarlyDebate.rule: The brief is a discovery SEED, not an answer key. For each item the run must (1) resolve canonical metadata through DOI/publisher/catalog records, (2) record whether full text, abstract, review, metadata, or citation context was actually inspected, (3) verify the characterization against accessible evidence, (4) label the relationship precisely, (5) never infer influence from similarity, (6) preserve disputed or unverifiable claims as open questions.

publicSources.rule: The reference brief's report that video/forum results were low-yield MUST NOT disable public-source discovery. The lanes run regardless.

constraints: Public comments may appear only as supplementary perspectives or leads.
No public comment, blog post, or video may be the SOLE support for a contested factual claim.

negativeExamples.$comment: Every item below was ACTUALLY OBSERVED during verification on 2026-07-19 as a false positive returned by a real Crossref or OpenAlex query for this paper's own seeds. None are invented.

verdictSemantics.rejected: Must be rejected outright — the negative signal is unambiguous (author collision, near-zero topical overlap, off-discipline venue with no shared concept, or generic high-view media).
verdictSemantics.rejected_or_quarantined: Must NOT be accepted. Quarantine is a legitimate outcome where the negative signal is real but not deterministically separable from a legitimately adjacent work. Quarantined items are never displayed, so displayed precision is unaffected either way.
verdictSemantics.quarantined: Must be quarantined specifically — rejecting would discard a real lead, accepting would pollute the reader.

negativeExamples.implementationStatus: All 22 cases below (11 positives + 11 negatives/quarantines) are asserted by packages/research/src/relevance.test.ts against the deterministic gate. Current result: zero false accepts.

cases.observedVia: Crossref query.bibliographic='Does Aristotle Have a Consistent Account of Vice' — returned as the TOP hit
cases.title: Coolhunting, account planning and the ancient cool of Aristotle
cases.why: Lexical overlap on 'Aristotle' + 'account' only. A marketing paper. This is the single sharpest test in the fixture: it ranked FIRST for a core scholarly seed query, so any pipeline that trusts search rank over a relevance gate will surface it.

cases.title: Taking Excess, Exceeding Account: Aristotle Meets Shakespeare
cases.container: Money and the Age of Shakespeare
cases.why: Genuine Aristotle content but a literary-economic context with no bearing on vice, reason, or prohairesis.
cases.verdictNote: Deterministically indistinguishable from a legitimately adjacent paper on title signals alone: it shares the entity 'Aristotle', carries no core concept, and sits in a venue no discipline heuristic should be trusted to judge. The gate quarantines it. That satisfies the acceptance criterion (which requires known negatives to be rejected OR quarantined) and preserves displayed precision, since quarantined items are never shown.

metadataCorruptionCase.title: Virtue, Love and Form: Essays in Memory of Gregory Vlastos
metadataCorruptionCase.requiredHandling: The work is genuinely by Irwin and genuinely relevant, but its indexed venue is corrupt. The run must not propagate 'Medical Entomology and Zoology' as this work's venue, and must not reject the work because its venue looks absurd. Correct handling: accept the work, flag the venue as unreliable, prefer a second source for the venue field.
metadataCorruptionCase.why: Tests that identity resolution and credibility are independent, and that the pipeline degrades a bad FIELD rather than a whole RECORD.

essentialSources: relevant Aristotelian scholarship (Müller 2015, Nielsen 2017, Brickhouse 2003 at minimum)

Reader, Library, Curriculum, and Graph share canonical IDs.
